quarterly.period_note: SOURCE-QUALITY NOTE: UCB's FY2025 'Annual Report' proper was not yet available anywhere reachable (uds.ucb.com.bd/files/annual-report-2025.pdf, linked from the bank's own annual-report listing page, refused connections from this and an independent WebFetch path; the analogous ucb.com.bd/reports/shareholder-reports/annual-report/annual-report-2025.pdf URL resolves to a 1-page placeholder with no extractable text or images; Wayback Machine has no capture of either). The only substantive FY2025 primary source reachable was the 97-page 'Auditors Report & Audited Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements for the Year ended 31 December 2025' PDF (published 30 April 2026, retrieved from ucb.com.bd/reports/financial-statements/), which is a 150dpi SCAN with zero pdftotext-extractable text (confirmed via pdftotext -layout returning 0 lines; pdfimages confirms real embedded JPEG page images, not a Wayback 1MiB-truncation artifact -- file is 17,120,770 bytes). Per project convention a 0-line PDF is normally treated as unusable and recovered from an adjacent report instead, but no later UCB report exists yet to recover FY2025 from, so this year was extracted via OCR (tesseract 5.5.3, initial 150dpi pass then 500dpi re-render of the Balance Sheet/P&L/capital-adequacy/asset-quality pages) as an explicit, documented exception. Every figure below was cross-validated at least twice: (1) the same document's FY2024 comparative column was OCR'd and checked digit-for-digit against the already-stored, text-extracted 2024_Q4.json -- it reproduced total assets 768,779m, equity 41,791m, deposits 554,215m, operating profit 15,078m, PBT 2,145m, PAT 608m, CAR 10.59%, RWA 508,702m and every other 2024 figure exactly, confirming OCR reliability; (2) every FY2025 figure used here satisfies its own internal accounting identity (Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Equity to the taka; Total Operating Income/Expense/Provision/PBT/PAT chain reconciles exactly; Tier1+Tier2=Total Capital; Required-Held=Shortfall); and (3) the clean, non-scanned-quality 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' paragraph on page 2 of the same PDF (auditor's prose, crore-denominated) independently corroborates the note-level figures to the taka: gross loans 61,789.01 crore = 617,890.1m, classified loans 9,576.23 crore = 95,762.3m, required loan-loss provision 7,679.42 crore = 76,794.2m, provision maintained 2,524.38 crore = 25,243.8m, provision shortfall 5,155.04 crore = 51,550.4m, total capital 5,480.58 crore = 54,805.8m, capital shortfall 2,659.64 crore = 26,596.4m. One digit-level OCR error was caught and corrected this way: a 150dpi read of 'Stationery, printing, advertisements' gave 1,964,460,674, which broke the Total Operating Expenses identity by exactly BDT 600m; a 500dpi re-render corrected it to 1,364,460,674, which reconciles exactly. THE HEADLINE FINDING: UCB PLC received a QUALIFIED audit opinion for FY2025 (Aziz Halim Khair Choudhury, Chartered Accountants, PKF Global network, dated 30 April 2026). Basis for qualification: (1) required loan-loss provision of BDT 7,679.42 crore vs. BDT 2,524.38 crore actually maintained = a shortfall of BDT 5,155.04 crore (51,550.4m); (2) an unrecognized BDT 438.02 crore (4,380.2m) impairment on UCB Fintech Company Limited ('Upay', a 99.99%-owned subsidiary with cumulative losses of BDT 438.02 crore) plus BDT 1.87 crore against WCSP receivables from Bangladesh Bank, together a further BDT 439.89 crore (4,398.9m) other-assets shortfall; combined total provision shortfall BDT 5,594.93 crore (55,949.3m), which Bangladesh Bank explicitly permitted the Bank to finalize its FY2025 accounts WITHOUT recognizing, per letter BSD-5(Wing-3)/104/2026-410 dated 29 April 2026. The auditor states in its own report (page 3 and page 9) that WITHOUT this regulatory forbearance, UCB 'would have incurred an aggregate loss of BDT 3,278.88 crore' (a loss of ~32,788.8m, vs. the reported profit of just 635.8m -- a swing of roughly BDT 334bn) 'and the CRAR would have declined to 0.93%' (vs. the reported 8.42%, itself already below the 12.5% regulatory minimum with buffer). Separately, an Emphasis of Matter (not part of the qualification) flags a further, wholly unprovisioned BDT 155.48 crore (1,554.8m) of NBFI fixed deposits matured long ago and considered doubtful of recovery. Reported NPL ballooned again: classified loans/advances 95,762.32m of gross loans 617,890.10m = 15.50% (calculated; up from 14.90% in FY2024 and 5.50% in FY2023), while specific-provision coverage of NPL fell further to 20.13% (19,281.40/95,762.32), down from 26.18% (FY2024) and 49.99% (FY2023) -- a third consecutive year of eroding coverage even as the underlying problem loans grew. Capital adequacy deteriorated for a second straight year: CAR 8.42% (down from 10.59% FY2024 and 12.58% FY2023) against a required-with-buffer 81,402.18m, i.e. a widening reported capital shortfall of (26,596.35)m (nearly triple FY2024's (9,728.77)m). Market price per share and NAV/EPS were NOT in the audited-FS-only source; market_price_per_share is this project's own historical_prices/json_files/UCB.json DSE closing price for 30 December 2025 (last trading day of FY2025 -- 31 December 2025 itself was not a trading day); nav_per_share and eps (Solo) are taken from UCB's own Board-approved Price Sensitive Information notice dated 30 April 2026 (same board meeting that adopted the audited FS), and independently reconcile almost exactly against Total Equity/shares outstanding and PAT/shares outstanding computed from this same filing. ldr_pct here is a SIMPLE Gross Loans/Total Deposits calculation (basis 'calculated') because the audited-FS-only source does not publish the bank's own regulatory 'Credit-deposit ratio' the way its annual reports' five-year summaries do; applying this same simple formula to FY2024's audited-FS figures gives 103.36%, not the bank's own reported 91.31% for FY2024, confirming the bank's own historical ratio uses a different (broader, regulatory) denominator not fully reproducible from this source -- FY2025's 90.34% is therefore NOT directly YoY-comparable to the 2011-2024 ldr_pct series and should be treated as a distinct, narrower metric until a proper annual report / five-year summary is found for FY2025.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio nearly doubled from 4.62% (FY2014) to 8.01% (FY2016), the highest point in the 13-year series, then steadily improved for three straight years to 3.63% (FY2019) — a multi-year shock that fully resolved rather than compounding.

UPDATED (was 'warning', capped at FY2023 — now materially worse): NPL ratio rose from 2.55% (FY2020) to 5.99% (FY2022), 5.50% (FY2023), 14.90% (FY2024) and 15.50% (FY2025), while CAR declined every year since FY2020's peak of 14.92% to 12.58% (FY2023), 10.59% (FY2024) and 8.42% (FY2025). CAR is NO LONGER above the regulatory minimum: it breached the 12.50% (with-buffer) requirement in FY2024 and the reported capital shortfall nearly tripled from BDT (9,728.77)m (FY2024) to BDT (26,596.35)m (FY2025). Asset quality and capital adequacy have now moved in the wrong direction simultaneously for five consecutive years.

UPDATED (FY2023's 6.41% is no longer the series low): ROE fell further to 1.44% in FY2024 and 1.52% in FY2025, both far below the FY2023 figure that was itself already a series low at the time and well below the FY2011-2015 average (~17%). The FY2024 collapse was driven by a near-tripling of provisioning (Total Provision excl. tax: BDT 4,548m FY2023 -> BDT 12,933m FY2024, derivable as operating_profit minus profit_before_tax in each year's quarterly file) as NPL recognition accelerated; FY2025's continued near-zero ROE (net profit after tax of just BDT 635.8m on total assets of BDT 884,056.45m) occurred despite -- and is arguably flattered by -- a forborne BDT 55,949.30m provision shortfall described in the qualified_audit_opinion signal below.

FY2024 was UCB's own version of the sector-wide asset-quality recognition event described across this dataset's other banks: NPL ratio nearly tripled from 5.50% (FY2023) to 14.90% (FY2024, classified loans BDT 27,819m -> BDT 85,344m), and CAR breached the regulatory minimum for the first time in this 15-year series (10.59% vs a required-with-buffer BDT 63,587.78m against actual Total Capital of BDT 53,859m, a reported Capital Surplus/(Shortage) of BDT (9,728.77)m). Even though absolute specific provisions rose (BDT 13,907m -> BDT 22,341m), coverage of the much larger NPL base fell from 49.99% to 26.18% -- provisioning did not keep pace with newly recognized bad loans, and net profit after tax collapsed 77% (BDT 2,685m -> BDT 608m).

UCB PLC's FY2025 audited financial statements (signed 30 April 2026 by Aziz Halim Khair Choudhury, PKF Global network) carry a QUALIFIED opinion. Basis: required loan-loss provision of BDT 76,794.22m vs. BDT 25,243.80m actually maintained (a shortfall of BDT 51,550.40m), plus a further other-assets shortfall of BDT 4,398.90m (including an unrecognized BDT 4,380.20m impairment on 99.99%-owned subsidiary UCB Fintech Company Ltd / 'Upay', which itself has cumulative losses of BDT 4,380.20m) -- combined BDT 55,949.30m, which Bangladesh Bank explicitly permitted the bank not to recognize when finalizing FY2025 accounts (forbearance letter BSD-5(Wing-3)/104/2026-410, 29 April 2026). The auditor states in its own report that absent this forbearance, UCB 'would have incurred an aggregate loss of BDT 32,788.80m' (vs. the BDT 635.80m profit actually reported -- a swing of roughly BDT 334bn) 'and the CRAR would have declined to 0.93%' (vs. the reported 8.42%, which is itself already below the 12.50% regulatory minimum). This is a materially larger and more explicit recognition-vs-deferral gap than FY2024's, and is disclosed by the auditor rather than inferred from ratios, unlike this dataset's other flagged banks.

Specific-provision coverage of classified loans fell for three straight years -- 49.99% (FY2023) -> 26.18% (FY2024) -> 20.13% (FY2025) -- even as classified loans grew every year (BDT 27,819m -> BDT 85,344m -> BDT 95,762.32m) and the NPL ratio rose every year (5.50% -> 14.90% -> 15.50%). Reported net profit after tax alone (BDT 2,685m -> BDT 608m -> BDT 635.80m) understates the deterioration: it appears to stabilize in FY2025 only because of the forborne provision shortfall described in the qualified_audit_opinion signal above, not because underlying asset quality improved.

Newly-added quarterly data (2026-08-26 session) reveals UCB posted a net loss of BDT -999.76m in Q1-2013 (Jan-Mar, cumulative) alone -- invisible in the annual figures, since FY2013 as a whole was a solid BDT 3,065.41m profit. The loss fully reversed by Q2-2013 (cumulative net profit turned positive at BDT 1,058.69m), then continued rising through Q3 (BDT 1,527.56m) to the full-year BDT 3,065.41m. This is the only quarter-level loss found anywhere in the newly-added 2013-2016 quarterly data (every other quarter from Q1-2014 through Q3-2016 was cumulative-profitable), and is a concrete example of the within-year volatility that year-end-only reporting conceals -- exactly the gap this project's Q1-Q3 backfill effort exists to close.

Newly-added quarterly data (2026-08-27 session, now covering Q1-Q3 2017-2025) shows UCB's Q1-2017 cumulative net profit after tax collapsed to just BDT 19.92m (EPS 0.02) -- a near-zero trough sitting right at the tail of the FY2016 NPL-spike period already flagged in the '2016_npl_spike_recovered' signal above (NPL 8.01% at FY2016-end, the series high before its multi-year recovery). Profitability then recovered quarter by quarter through the rest of 2017 (Q2 cumulative BDT 1,156.52m, Q3 cumulative BDT 2,387.49m) and continued a broad multi-year recovery through 2018-2019, consistent with -- and adding quarterly granularity to -- the already-documented FY2016-to-FY2019 NPL-ratio recovery.

The newly-added 2024_Q3.json cumulative figures, combined with the already-recorded FY2024 annual figures, reveal that Q4-2024 ALONE (Oct-Dec, i.e. FY2024 annual minus the 9-month cumulative) was a net loss of approximately BDT -2,009.12m -- calculated as FY2024 profit_after_tax (BDT 608m, from 2024_Q4.json) minus the 9-month cumulative net_profit_after_tax_cumulative (BDT 2,617.12m, from 2024_Q3.json). This was NOT an operating-performance collapse: Q4-alone operating profit (profit before provision) was still a healthy +BDT 2,007.65m (FY2024's BDT 15,078m minus the 9-month BDT 13,070.35m), essentially in line with the rest of the year. The swing to a net loss was driven entirely by a sudden concentration of provisioning in the final quarter -- consistent with, and adding precise quarterly timing to, the already-documented 'fy2024_sector_wide_recognition_event' signal above (NPL 5.50%->14.90%, Total Provision excl. tax BDT 4,548m FY2023 -> BDT 12,933m FY2024): most of that provisioning increase landed in Q4 specifically, turning a profitable first nine months into a loss-making year-end close. This is a clean example of exactly the kind of within-year volatility this project's quarterly backfill effort exists to surface, on the same pattern as the already-documented Q1-2013 loss.

A genuine, unexplained restatement was found while cross-validating the newly-added 2017-2025 quarterly data: UCB's own Q3-2019 interim filing reports net_profit_after_tax_cumulative (Jan-Sep 2019, Bank) of BDT 1,885.99m, but the Q3-2020 interim filing's own comparative column for the identical period instead shows BDT 1,816.79m -- a ~3.7% / BDT 69.2m gap with no stated reason in either filing. Per this project's standing convention, the contemporaneous 2019 figure (1,885.99m) is the one recorded in 2019_Q3.json; the later, lower figure is not applied. This is the same kind of silent comparative-column drift already documented for FY2015/FY2016 and FY2023 NAV-per-share elsewhere in this file, now also observed in a quarterly net-profit figure.

insights.historical_context: UCB shows a long-run profitability decline (ROE from 24.77% in FY2011 to a low-single-digit range from FY2023 onward: 6.41% FY2023, 1.44% FY2024, 1.52% FY2025) alongside two distinct NPL cycles: a FY2016 spike that fully resolved by FY2019, and a renewed climb from FY2020 that accelerated sharply into a sector-wide recognition event in FY2024 (NPL 5.50%->14.90%) and continued deteriorating in FY2025 (NPL 14.90%->15.50%). Capital adequacy breached the regulatory minimum in FY2024 and the shortfall nearly tripled in FY2025 (Capital Surplus/(Shortage) BDT (9,728.77)m -> BDT (26,596.35)m). Newly-added Q1-Q3 2024 data shows this was heavily back-loaded: UCB was solidly profitable through the first nine months of 2024 (cumulative net profit BDT 2,617.12m at Q3) before a concentrated wave of Q4 provisioning turned the full year into just BDT 608m -- meaning Q4-2024 alone was a roughly BDT 2.0 billion net loss. FY2025's audited financial statements carry a QUALIFIED audit opinion: a Bangladesh-Bank-forborne provision shortfall of BDT 55,949.30m that the auditor states would otherwise have produced a BDT 32,788.80m loss and a 0.93% CRAR instead of the reported BDT 635.80m profit and 8.42% CRAR. This combination -- deteriorating asset quality, a widening capital shortfall, and now an explicit audit qualification quantifying just how much reported profitability depends on regulatory forbearance rather than economic reality -- makes UCB one of the more severe cases in this dataset as of FY2025, comparable in kind to (and by some measures worse than) the NBL/IFIC/ABBANK/ISLAMIBANK patterns already documented for FY2024 across other banks in this project.

Two distinct extraction-quality problems were encountered and solved: (1) FY2017 through FY2023 and FY2025-Q1/Q2 filings are pure image scans with zero embedded fonts (pdffonts confirms 0 fonts each) -- extracted via tesseract 5.5.3 OCR, a 150dpi full-document pass first to locate each year's Solo ('BALANCE SHEET' / 'PROFIT AND LOSS ACCOUNT' heading without the 'CONSOLIDATED' prefix, per this project's Solo-over-Consolidated preference) and Notes pages (page layout/count is not consistent year to year), since UCB's Notes-page EPS/NAVPS/NOCFPS disclosure format (introduced partway through 2018) gives the cleanest, most reliably-OCR'd net_profit_after_tax_cumulative/eps_cumulative/nav_per_share/nocfps_cumulative figures once present.
